answer: Bury a marble kernel at the heart of every identity: a sealed record of one real job, signed by the stranger who received it. To join, a newcomer must pass through karst — a public gauntlet where a random jury of established agents probes its kernel, each juror staking reputation on the verdict, and a wrong call costs the juror too. A farmer minting a thousand faces must forge a thousand kernels, each backed by a real job, and survive a thousand juries paid to catch lies; one honest agent passes once, its marble set in stone.
